principles: Canonical public package names should match the Lattice product identity.
Legacy compatibility should be explicit, bounded, and testable rather than hidden in stale hard-coded strings.
Runtime/process facts that gates consume must be updated mechanically with code, docs, and verification scripts together.
Avoid broad prose churn beyond package identity unless a stale Koala reference would confuse users or diagnostics.
drivers: The user does not want @koala-agent/* to remain the visible package identity.
The repo still supports older projects and koala command aliases, so abrupt removal could break existing wrappers.
Hard-coded package paths affect doctor/runtime checks, worktree cleanup, generated bootstrap, and Codex adapter verification.

options.name: A: Make @lattice-agent/* canonical with @koala-agent/* legacy fallback
pros: Solves the visible package-name problem while keeping existing projects recoverable.
Keeps the change focused on identity and compatibility surfaces.
Allows runtime diagnostics to explain canonical versus legacy paths.
cons: Requires more code changes than editing package.json only.
Some legacy Koala references intentionally remain and must be clearly labeled.

options.name: B: Hard rename everything and remove all Koala aliases
pros: Cleanest branding surface after the change.
cons: Likely breaks existing local wrappers, docs, hooks, and user muscle memory immediately.
Too broad for this request because it changes command/runtime compatibility, not just package identity.

options.name: C: Only edit packages/main/package.json name
pros: The immediate npm metadata display changes.
cons: Runtime checks and generated wrappers still point to @koala-agent/core.
Package-lock and dependent package metadata would drift.
Doctor/verification scripts could fail or report misleading package facts.

chosen: A: Make @lattice-agent/* canonical with @koala-agent/* legacy fallback
rationale: Choose the canonical-plus-fallback rename because the user wants Koala removed from public package identity, but the existing system has many package-path consumers where a hard break would create avoidable failures. This keeps Lattice as the visible name while making legacy behavior explicit and verifiable.

preMortem.scenario: Package manager metadata becomes internally inconsistent
preMortem.trigger: package.json names change but package-lock or workspace dependency entries still use @koala-agent names
preMortem.consequence: Install, build, or published tarball metadata continues to show Koala or fails dependency resolution
preMortem.mitigation: Update package-lock files and run metadata assertions across all workspace package.json/package-lock files.

preMortem.scenario: Runtime doctor/relink checks can no longer find the global package
preMortem.trigger: hard-coded path join(..., @koala-agent, core) is replaced incompletely or without fallback
preMortem.consequence: worktree cleanup, doctor, and Codex adapter checks produce false warnings or fail in existing installations
preMortem.mitigation: Introduce canonical constants/helpers for @lattice-agent/core and bounded @koala-agent/core fallback, then update verification scripts.

preMortem.trigger: agent templates or adapter assets import @koala-agent/core but CHK-004 verification omits verify_codex
preMortem.consequence: adapter gate sees stale package identity or generated prompts still teach old package imports
preMortem.mitigation: Include node bin/lattice.js verify_codex when templates or adapter assets are touched, matching INIT reviewer advisory.

preMortem.scenario: Branding cleanup expands into unrelated product rename
preMortem.trigger: global search for Koala leads to broad docs and historical compatibility rewrites
preMortem.consequence: Large noisy diff risks breaking legacy command semantics and obscures the actual package-scope fix
preMortem.mitigation: Limit code changes to package identity, canonical runtime references, and docs that present public package names; leave clearly legacy aliases labeled.
